A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe dnaHNet, with matching main sections and Appendices A.1–A.4. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison; v3 adds Appendix A.5 and Figure 7.

before.justification: v1 reports original scaling experiments, MaveDB variant-effect predictions, DEG gene-essentiality predictions, and biological segmentation analyses in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds measured GPU throughput, memory consumption, and forward-pass latency in Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same hierarchical architecture, boundary routing, smoothing, compression targets, training objective, and inference procedure. The new benchmark evaluates existing model variants.

E1.justification: GTDB pretraining and the MaveDB, DEG, and B. subtilis evaluations are unchanged. The added efficiency benchmark varies sequence lengths and model configurations without introducing a new biological dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: StripedHyena2 and Transformer baselines remain in their existing comparisons. Appendix A.5 benchmarks the already-used StripedHyena2 family; its 100M, 167M, and 234M configurations do not introduce a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a hardware benchmark using BF16 forward passes on one NVIDIA H100, testing three dnaHNet variants and three StripedHyena2 sizes across lengths from 2^10 to 2^19 nucleotides. Throughput, peak memory, and latency supplement the existing FLOP evaluation; earlier protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new analysis tests whether theoretical FLOP savings translate into practical efficiency and examines how throughput, memory, and latency vary with sequence length and model scale. Existing hierarchy comparisons and biological segmentation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised. Figure 7 presents measurements without error bars or timing-repetition information.

E6.justification: Figure 7 substantially extends the efficiency evidence with the first measured throughput, memory, and latency results. Reported examples include dnaHNet-M exceeding 1.6 million tokens/sec and dnaHNet-XL using about 18 GB versus over 55 GB for SH2-100M at 2^19 nucleotides. The plots also show SH2 faster at short lengths. Existing scaling and downstream results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations 1–4, and hierarchical FLOP-scaling argument are unchanged. The hardware benchmark adds no mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficiency, zero-shot prediction, and learned biological hierarchy. The new benchmark supplies additional evidence without revising those core claims.

C2.justification: Figure 7's caption newly attributes the longest-context throughput decline to memory pressure, connects reduced memory use to longer-context feasibility, and interprets measured speed advantages as consequences of hierarchical compression. Existing biological interpretations and Section 5.1 limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 specifies the new benchmark's single H100 GPU, BF16 precision, and forward-pass workload. Existing architecture and training details remain unchanged. Benchmark batch size, timing warmup, and repetition details are not supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to H-Net and other genomic tokenization approaches are unchanged. Appendix A.5 introduces no additional citations.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short Appendix A.5 and explanatory caption, updates author affiliations and dates, and corrects three figure references in Section 4.3. The existing prose and overall section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-panel Figure 7 with legends and a detailed caption, and shifts Table 6 upward on the final page. Existing figures and tables retain their content and design; the front matter also undergoes limited reflow.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.5 adds useful measured evidence for long-context efficiency beyond v1's FLOP estimates, and corrected figure references improve navigation. The benefit is limited by incomplete timing details and an overstated Figure 7 caption: its claim of higher throughput across all lengths conflicts with the plotted short-context advantage for StripedHyena2. Overall, the added evidence provides a limited net improvement.
